description.narrative: Kurigram, in northwestern Bangladesh, is highly exposed to recurring floods, river erosion, and climate-induced hazards. These disproportionately impact marginalized groups—women, children, persons with disabilities, and agriculture-dependent families. To address this, Christian Aid proposes an anticipatory intervention in the most at-risk unions of Rowmari and Nageshwari upazilas, focusing on preparedness and early actions. Project Location Targeted unions were selected through contingency planning and Start Fund coordination, guided by GloFAS and FFWC forecasts: Rowmari Upazila: Saulmari, Raumari, Jadur Char, Dantbhanga, Bandaber Nageshwari Upazila: Ballabher Khas Approach The project follows an inclusive, equitable, and community-centered approach, prioritizing: · People in extreme poverty · Persons with disabilities and the elderly · Young women, adolescents, and pregnant/lactating mothers · Ethnic minorities and marginalized groups · Women migrant workers Key Outputs · Vulnerable communities take pre-emptive actions to protect lives/assets · Improved community and institutional capacity for early response Core Activities 1. Community Engagement: Orientation for staff on code of conduct, inclusion, and safeguarding. Awareness sessions on cash use and early actions. Inception meetings with local stakeholders. 2. Early Warning: Timely flood warnings will be disseminated via miking and door-to-door outreach with support from FPP and UDMCs. 3. Health Kits at Shelters: Six shelters will receive sanitary pads and first aid kits to support basic health and hygiene, especially for displaced women and girls. 4. Shelter Repair & Safety: Repairs will enhance safety at 6 shelters. Charger lights and batteries will be provided for night-time protection. 5. Food & Livelihood Support: · 900 dry food packages (150 per shelter) with items like flattened rice, sugar, biscuits, ORS · 300 cattle feed packages (50 per shelter) · 12 temporary cattle sheds to safeguard livestock 6. Cash Assistance: A total of 1,415 households will each receive BDT 5,000 via mobile transfer (bKash) to enable anticipatory actions such as securing homes, storing essentials, and protecting livestock. 7. Monitoring & Accountability: Joint monitoring using Start Fund tools will evaluate effectiveness and utilization. A Complaint and Feedback Response Mechanism (CFRM) will ensure transparency and responsiveness to community input.
